title: missed the recital for a static fire, how do I make it right

messages.content: missed Δ-9's recital for static fire test which then slipped, feel like a terrible dad

It sounds like you're feeling a lot of guilt right now. Missing important moments can be really tough, especially when they don't go as planned anyway. What about this made you feel like a terrible dad?
dad always let work take priority, promised myself I'd never do that

I understand. Those early experiences can shape how we see ourselves as parents. It's clear you care deeply about your family. What do you think could help you balance these responsibilities better, moving forward?
need a way to be present even when things are busy, how do other people manage it?

Many people find that scheduling family time as non-negotiable can help. It could also be useful to delegate more at work when big personal events are coming up. Have you talked to Priya Chen about blocking out some time?
haven't yet, but probably should. what about apologizing to Δ-9?

An honest, heartfelt apology can go a long way. Let them know how important they are to you and that you're committed to being there next time. Kids appreciate when parents acknowledge their feelings sincerely.
worried about becoming too much like dad, any tips on changing that pattern?

It's about conscious choices. Reflect on what you wish had been different with your dad and how you can create those changes. Building habits of checking in with yourself can also help shift long-term patterns.
makes sense, old habits die hard though. how can i keep family a priority during big launches?

Planning ahead can create more flexibility during busy periods. Set firm boundaries for family time, even if it's just a short daily check-in. Communicating these intentions to your team might also rally them to help you achieve this balance.
i'm afraid space will always be the 'big thing', how do i explain that to them?

Being open about your passion for space while emphasizing that it doesn't diminish your love for your family might help. Share why it's important to you and how you want them to be part of the journey too, in a way that includes them.
i want them to understand but not feel secondary

That’s a delicate balance. Perhaps involving them in your work in small ways, like showing them the rockets, can help them feel related to what you do. Meanwhile, prioritize special family traditions to reinforce their importance in your life.
traditions could be something, always thought they were too rigid

Traditions need not be rigid. They can be as simple as a weekly game night or cooking a favorite meal together. The key is creating something meaningful you all look forward to, which reinforces connection.
thanks, feel a bit better. guess it’s back to first principles parenting

It sounds like you're already on the right track by reflecting and seeking solutions. Parenting, like rocket science, involves constant learning and adjustments. You're approaching it with care and thoughtfulness.
alright, gonna try to get some sleep, talk to priya in the morning
That sounds like a good plan. Rest well. These steps will help you make more room for family amidst the excitement and pressures of your work. You've got this.
